audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer never mentions Goes Where He Pleases, the passive that decides whether Galio's entire kit works, and it never states what Heart Zapper actually does. It also opens with 'Respect the physical damage — build the armor side', which is not what the kit says.
audit.why: Riot's passive text: 'Dr. Mundo resists the first Immobilizing effect that hits him, instead losing Health and dropping a chemical cannister nearby. Dr. Mundo can pick it up by walking over it, restoring Health and reducing this Ability's Cooldown.' A Galio whose whole value is a taunt and a knock-up has to spend a throwaway immobilise first or the real one is eaten. Heart Zapper 'stor[es] a portion of damage he takes... deals a burst of damage to nearby enemies. If the burst hit an enemy, he heals' — so poking him while it runs literally pays for his heal. And his bonus attack damage comes from Blunt Force Trauma, which is what makes armour relevant, not a blanket 'physical damage' claim.
audit.corrected: Passive and Heart Zapper written into the tldr, winCon, trade lines, cooldown block, do's, don'ts and the key-interactions slot; the armour line tied to Blunt Force Trauma.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole full layer is built on 'trade when Heart Zapper is down' with no number, and treats Infected Bonesaw as if it had a punishable cooldown.
audit.why: Heart Zapper is 17s at rank 1 and costs him nothing; Infected Bonesaw is a flat 4s at 975 range at every rank, so there is no window to wait out — you stay outside 975 or you eat it. Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s.
audit.corrected: 17s, 4s and 120s all stated, and the Bonesaw advice changed from waiting to spacing.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why calls Stormsurge/Riftmaker your spike on a stage the chart gives Mundo, and phases[4].why ends with the boilerplate 'Reassess his ultimate too'.
audit.why: His spikes are Heart Zapper at 2, Maximum Dosage at 6 and every health item after; Galio's only real spike here is level 1 and the level-6 roam.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization says 'Oblivion Orb early — his healing fights your trade math' without naming a source, and leaves boots as a coin flip.
audit.why: The healing is Heart Zapper's burst and Maximum Dosage's missing-health heal plus regen — both worth naming so the player knows anti-heal is not optional. His bonus AD is Blunt Force Trauma, which makes Plated Steelcaps the boot.
audit.corrected: Both heal sources named and the boot resolved.

audit.why: Both charts agree — Skill at 1, Mundo at 2 and 3, Skill at 4-5 and 6, Mundo at both item rows — and the content prose argues exactly that shape, ending on 'the verdict is even because the lane is a stalemate you tilt your way through the map'. At 48.57% over 35 games that reads honestly, so I changed no stage.

You will not solo-kill a drain-tank, so stop trying; instead flag a flank into a winning lane or onto his jungler and use your global to make this a map game. notes: drmundo.json's resistances-invalidated entry in _missing-interactions is built on Maximum Dosage, but that ability bypasses nothing — it heals. I did not write a resistance-bypass claim. Riot's text gives no damage type for Infected Bonesaw, so I attributed the armour case to Blunt Force Trauma's bonus attack damage only. Whether Mundo's passive can be baited by a summoner-spell CC or only by champion CC is not in any local file; I wrote 'a cheap immobilise' without specifying.
